style: Say warmly with a gravelly voice, like an old ranger who keeps a field guide in his pocket.
lines: Tap a specimen. Then tap the first and last word where the reasoning goes wrong.
Now tap a species in your field kit, or tap Legit. Then tap Log sighting.
Legit ones still look like something. Tap the species it resembles.
Not quite. Read the note, or tap Field test.
Logged.
Studied, not counted. Tap another specimen, or open Guide to review your notes.
Your field guide. A card is confirmed when you have caught it and let its twin go. Tap a card to open it.
Choose a species in the menu. Write at least eight words in The fallacy and Its fair twin.
Tap the first and last word to mark the reasoning. Use arrow keys to move between words, and Enter to mark.
Now tap the last word of the field mark.
Tap Log sighting to check your mark and call.
Read the field question. Tap Yes or No to see what that answer suggests.
Write at least eight words in The fallacy and Its fair twin.
Tap Mark words on an unmarked slip. Then tap its first and last field-mark word.
Tap the first and last word of the field mark on this slip.
Tap Field test it to test both slips.
Tap Close to return to your work.
Answer the field question for the fallacy slip, then for its fair twin. Tap Yes or No.
Tap another specimen, or open Guide to examine your sightings.
Tap Show me to study the field mark and call. A revealed sighting does not count.

Straw man: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
Would the other side say 'yes, that is what I mean'?
Black-or-white: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
Are there really only these two choices?
Slippery slope: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
Is there a reason given for each step, and is the ending likely?
Hasty generalization: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
How many cases, and were they chosen fairly?
Unqualified authority: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
Is this person an expert on this exact question?
Bandwagon: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
Is the claim about how popular something is, or about whether it is good or true?
Post hoc: confirmed. You can tell it from its twin.
Was anything else different, and was there a comparison?
Yes means popularity itself. No means a claim about quality or truth.
Yes means enough fairly chosen cases. No means too few cases or unfair selection.
Yes means a fair comparison accounts for other differences. No means sequence alone.
